_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); discount-retail signals

pit_profile.why: Walmart: 'is a people-led, technology-powered omni-channel retailer dedicated to helping people around the world save money and live better by providing the opportunity to shop in both retail stores and through eCommerce, and to access our other service offerings'; 'everyday low prices ("EDLP")'; 'We operate in a highly competitive omni-channel retail industry in all of the markets we serve' ('We face strong competition from other retailers, wholesale club operators, omni-channel retailers and other businesses which could materially adversely affect our financial performance'); and 'General economic conditions and other economic factors, globally or in one or more of the markets we serve, may adversely affect our financial performance' (its own FY2025 10-K): a low-price store network whose demand follows the consumer economy by its own account; ECOMMERCE is live (from 2015-01-01) and its competition risk factor puts it on the watch list: company-acknowledged, with no dated evidence that the market prices it for Walmart

theme_watch.reason: Live: Walmart's own FY2025 10-K says 'Each of our segments competes for customers, employees, digital prominence, products and services and in other important aspects of its business with many other local, regional, national and global physical, eCommerce and omni-channel retailers, social commerce platforms, wholesale club operators and retail intermediaries, as well as companies that offer services in digital advertising, data analytics/insights, fulfillment and delivery services, health and wellness and financial services.' At the same time it sells online itself: 'Walmart U.S. eCommerce sales positively contributed approximately 2.9% and 2.6% to comparable sales for fiscal 2025 and 2024'. The stock trades at 40.1x FY26E — a premium. The theme registry dates the market's pricing of e-commerce to 2017-06-16 (Amazon agrees to buy Whole Foods; grocers and food retailers sell off the same day), evidence that names no company. Re-file as DISRUPTION_EXPOSED (ECOMMERCE) only if dated evidence shows the market pricing online substitution of Walmart's store sales specifically.

classification.quality_note: Walmart: 'is a people-led, technology-powered omni-channel retailer dedicated to helping people around the world save money and live better by providing the opportunity to shop in both retail stores and through eCommerce, and to access our other service offerings'; 'everyday low prices ("EDLP")'; 'We operate in a highly competitive omni-channel retail industry in all of the markets we serve' ('We face strong competition from other retailers, wholesale club operators, omni-channel retailers and other businesses which could materially adversely affect our financial performance'); and 'General economic conditions and other economic factors, globally or in one or more of the markets we serve, may adversely affect our financial performance' (its own FY2025 10-K): a low-price store network whose demand follows the consumer economy by its own account; ECOMMERCE is live (from 2015-01-01) and its competition risk factor puts it on the watch list: company-acknowledged, with no dated evidence that the market prices it for Walmart. durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price rich; +123% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap -2.10; conservative 2yr -39%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -5.9%/yr (worst year FY16-FY25, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +6.2%/yr (Q3 guide + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +6.2%/yr (FY16-FY25 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +14.5%/yr (best 2-yr run FY16-FY25); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: WMT (retrospective, 2025-09-26) ✕ AVOID — Ratio B infx (64.1% downside to Bear $37 / +-32.1% upside to Bull $70) | Adj composite 1.67 vs market 3.77: gap -2.10 [OVERVALUED] | +123% above the EPP floor $46 (18x FY26E $2.57) | Conservative 2-yr case: -38.6% total (-19.3%/yr) | At 40.1x FY26E the 15% hurdle price $136 sits above the BULL case; U.S. comps +4.3% in Q2 FY26, forward sales +3.75-4.75% (Q3 FY26 net sales guide at constant currency); e-commerce competition is live and company-acknowledged; no dated evidence ties the multiple to it.
